question: Does one fixed volatility exposure rule improve on a calibration risk-scaled static allocation, rather than merely reducing equity exposure?
sample_status: These years were used in earlier research. This is a new exploratory mechanism check, not an untouched holdout or prospective validation.
weight: min(1, target / prior_close_20_market_day_sample_std_annualized); zero volatility gives weight 1; no leverage or shorts
rebalance: First market session each month at proxy open, using only previous market close information; initial evaluation session included. Hold proxy units and cash between rebalances.
missing_quote_policy: Retain full market calendar. Missing open/close is untradable; carry last observed close solely for valuation. Volatility needs 20 consecutive valid adjacent-session returns; missing window skips rebalance, holds units/cash, no queued order. Report missing valuation dates and underestimate-of-intrahalt-drawdown risk.
static_comparator: Fixed min(1, target / 2023 sample annualized close-return volatility); monthly constant mix, same costs. This is calibration risk scaling, not exact ex-post equal realized risk.
cost_status: Hypothetical all-in proportional cost scenarios, not asserted tax/commission rates; charge initial acquisition and all rebalances; no terminal liquidation, report remaining exposure.
return_status: Forward official-reference adjusted quote proxy, not shareholder cash ledger, total return or executable fill. No backward adjusted columns. Synthetic proxy-unit accounting only.
go_gate: At both cost scenarios: dynamic CAGR strictly exceeds calibration-static CAGR, close maximum drawdown magnitude is no larger, and mean/volatility is higher; at least two of the three calendar subperiods have higher dynamic return. Passing only authorizes a separate independent-data proposal, never deployment.
stop_gate: If go_gate fails, close this exact rule without parameter/threshold search, wider downloads, fitted models or daily validation. If it passes, record proxy and short-sample limitations before any separately frozen follow-up.
